source.title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems

accepted.question_text: For homogeneous and isotropic universes governed by the basic gravi-dilaton effective string action with higher-order and loop corrections neglected, what are the detailed asymptotic limits, and are the known dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion solutions asymptotically stable?

evidence.quote: 2.1 Asymptotics of specific tree-level string actions I The aim here is to describe the detailed asymptotic limits of universes obeying the basic gravi-dilaton effective string action, neglecting higher order and loop corrections. The plan to give a complete asymptotic analysis of the NS-NS models and first results about the asymptotic stability of the known solutions (dilaton-moduli-vacuum and axion solutions).

accepted.question_text: For string cosmologies with RR fields, what are the asymptotic properties of the universes, are the known solutions stable and unique, and do there exist asymptotic solutions that appear only subdominantly and thereby constrain the possible singular asymptotic behaviours?

evidence.quote: 2.2 Asymptotics of specific tree-level string actions II The problem here is to study the asymptotic properties of universes with RR fields. This asymptotic analysis will tell us about the stability of the known solutions, whether they are unique. It is possible that there are solutions which exist only subdominantly asymptotically and these are expected to be identified by our analysis.

accepted.question_text: When anisotropies are incorporated into simple anisotropic string cosmologies with NS-NS and/or RR fields, what asymptotic decompositions occur, can lower-parameter families still attract other solution families, and how do asymptotic cancellations organize the overall solution space?

evidence.quote: 2.3 Asymptotics of specific tree-level string actions III The next step is to incorporate anisotropies into the asymptotic regimes and study simple anisotropic models with NS-NS and/or RR fields. There will be many decompositions of the vector field asymptotically and there may be solutions with a smaller number of arbitrary constants which still attract other families of solutions. We expect here the phenomenon of asymptotic cancellations to occur.

accepted.question_text: For the exact cosmological solutions known in heterotic M-theory and Horava-Witten cosmology with nontrivial Ramond fields, what is the full asymptotic significance of those solutions, and what is the dimension of the asymptotic attractor that they form?

evidence.quote: 2.4 Asymptotics of M-theory cosmology It is very important that there are some exact cosmological solutions in heterotic M-theory and Horava-Witten cosmology (with nontrivial Ramond fields) found in the papers of Lucas-Ovrut-Waldram ... An asymptotic analysis along the lines mentioned in this paper is expected to reveal for the first time the full significance of these solutions and especially the dimension of the asymptotic attractor they form.

accepted.question_text: Are the cosmological solutions associated with a BPS state stable when one allows the solutions to be inhomogeneous, and how might that stability affect the ambient cosmological construction?

evidence.quote: 2.5 Asymptotics of M-theory cosmology II This is an extension of the previous problem in a different direction. The plan is to examine the stability of those cosmological solutions that are associated with a BPS state cf. [50]. This requires the solutions to be inhomogeneous, and so may also have a significant role to play in the ambient cosmological construction.

accepted.question_text: For the stable solutions obtained in the preceding string- and M-theory cosmology problems, what do full inhomogeneous perturbations show about their genericity, and what does a generic analytic solution with the same qualitative characteristics look like?

evidence.quote: 2.6 Genericity issues in string and M-theory cosmology For stable solutions found in the previous two problems, a genericity analysis to the full inhomogeneous perturbations may be applied. One expects in this way to discover what any generic solution sharing such characteristics will look like, at least for the analytic case.

accepted.question_text: If one studies the full corrected action (3.1) for flat or curved FRW universes, including the dilaton term and its coupling to higher-order curvature terms, what asymptotic behaviours and stability properties arise, in particular for the stability of the vacuum state in this effective string theory?

evidence.quote: 3.1 Asymptotics of gravi-dilaton flat FRW cosmologies The plan in this project is to extend relevant asymptotic analysis and stability results ... to the case of the full action (3.1), that is including the dilaton term and its coupling to the higher-order curvature terms. This will provide especially important results for the stability of the vacuum in this effective string theory.

accepted.question_text: In the basic string effective theory with quantum corrections and a general fluid coupled to the dilaton, what are all of the stable asymptotic solutions?

evidence.quote: 3.2 Extensions to general tree-level cosmology for any fluid parameter For the basic string effective theory with quantum corrections, find all stable asymptotic solutions with a general fluid coupled to the dilaton.

accepted.question_text: How do the known single-fluid results for flat string cosmologies change when the model is replaced by two interacting, fairly general fluids that exchange energy, and which previously known asymptotic results remain valid in that broader setting?
accepted.context_brief: Interacting fluids in flat string cosmology

evidence.quote: 3.3 Interacting fluids in flat string cosmology The aim of this project is to examine how all known single fluid results in flat string cosmologies generalize to the case of two interacting, more or less general fluids which exchange energy. This is very important because it will reveal which results remain in such a generalized situation.

accepted.question_text: For curved string cosmologies with interacting fluids and higher-order curvature corrections, what asymptotic behaviours occur, especially when curvature is asymptotically dominant in some regimes and asymptotically subdominant in others?

evidence.quote: 3.4 Curved string cosmologies with interactions This deals with the important case of curved universes with interacting fluids in string cosmologies with higher order curvature corrections. We expect to see the effects of dominant as well as subdominant curvature asymptotically.

accepted.question_text: When the 11-dimensional supergravity or M-theory action is deformed by higher-order Lovelock and Weyl terms, are the resulting exact cosmological solutions stable, what asymptotic modes of the fields are possible, and can one obtain a no-hair theorem for an inflationary stage in M-theory?

evidence.quote: 3.5 Stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmology I ... when the M-theory action is further deformed to include Lovelock and Weyl terms [65, 66], there are several exact solutions not present in standard M-theory cosmologies. Are these solutions stable? In this problem one expects to trace all possible asymptotic modes of the fields, and in this way to give the first reliable results about the possibility of a no-hair theorem for an inflationary stage in M-theory.

accepted.question_text: Are the deformed M-theory power-law cosmological solutions asymptotically stable, and what would the answer imply for the naturalness of inflation in M-theory cosmology?

evidence.quote: 3.6 Stability of 11-dimensional supergravity cosmology II Here the plan is to study the asymptotic stability of the deformed M-theory power-law cosmological solutions [65, 66]. This is especially important for the naturalness of inflation in M-theory cosmology.

accepted.question_text: For a three-dimensional Robertson-Walker brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk, what singularity structure and asymptotic behaviour occur, do regular solutions exist, and can such solutions help address the cosmological constant problem through the self-tuning proposal?

evidence.quote: 4.1 RW branes and scalar fields The singularity structure and the corresponding asymptotic behavior of a 3D RW brane coupled to a scalar field in a five-dimensional bulk can be analyzed in full generality ... One central issue is to examine the existence of regular solutions, and in accordance with the self-tuning proposal, to address the cosmological constant problem.

accepted.question_text: When a perfect fluid is included in Robertson-Walker brane cosmology, can one find a regular bulk solution that both localizes gravity on the brane and satisfies the null energy condition in the bulk?

evidence.quote: 4.2 RW branes with perfect fluid ... the issue of finding a regular bulk solution is further complicated by the existence of extra constraints, namely, how to localize gravity on the brane and at the same time meet the requirements of the null energy condition in the bulk.

accepted.question_text: If the bulk theory allows interactions between a scalar field and a fluid, do those interactions produce regular asymptotics, and can the resulting interacting-fluid models satisfy all three conditions discussed in the preceding brane problem?

evidence.quote: 4.3 RW branes with interactions ... This project will search the question as to whether regular asymptotics are the result of the interactions between the scalar field and the fluid. It would be interesting to test whether interacting fluids can meet all three conditions discussed in the previous problem.

accepted.question_text: Under general inhomogeneous perturbations, are the asymptotic brane solutions stable, and what does function counting imply about the degree of generality of the resulting brane asymptotics?

evidence.quote: 4.4 Genericity of the asymptotic solutions In this project the aim is to examine, through a generic perturbation analysis, whether the found solutions are stable when we consider general inhomogeneous perturbations. Through function counting, we may be able to conclude about the degree of generality of the found brane asymptotics.

accepted.question_text: In string theories with higher-order corrections and matter described by a general fluid equation of state, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable when the higher-order terms enter only subdominantly, so that it can serve as a viable model for passage through the singularity in ekpyrotic or cyclic scenarios?

evidence.quote: 4.5 Ekpyrosis and the Milne state with asymptotically subdominant higher-order terms This project aims to examine the global asymptotic stability of the Milne state in string theories with higher-order corrections in an effort to decide as to whether or not this state is a viable representative of the passage through the singularity in models with an ekpyrotic or cyclic phase.

accepted.question_text: In the ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios of M-theory, is the Milne state globally asymptotically stable when the higher-order terms enter dominantly during the evolution, and what does that imply for both ekpyrosis and M-theory cosmology more broadly?

evidence.quote: 4.6 Ekpyrosis and the Milne state with asymptotically dominant higher-order terms This is a continuation of the previous problem concerning the asymptotic global stability of the Milne state in the Ekpyrotic and cyclic scenarios in M-theory. However, this time one is interested in the effects of the higher-order terms now entering dominantly in the evolution.

evidence.quote: g5 cannot be continued to arbitrary values in the y-dimension without some sort of matching; all flat brane solutions are singular at a finite, arbitrary y-distance from the position of the brane located at y = 0. The generic curved problem is under investigation.

needs_review.question_text_raw: This is something left to future work.

evidence.quote: Therefore it seems that our construction is admitted by all conformally related perturbations of Minkowski space. This is something left to future work.

needs_review.question_text_raw: It is possible (although not clear at present) that our construction bears some relation to twistor space.

evidence.quote: 6.9 Relation to twistors It is possible (although not clear at present) that our construction bears some relation to twistor space, in particular, the space PN - the null projective twistor 5-space.

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record to the arXiv v2 PDF for the same work because the zbMATH page exposed the exact title and an arXiv full-text link; mapped the paper and identified sections 2, 3, and 4 as the primary open-problem regions.
Extracted six explicit open problems from subsections 2.1-2.6 on tree-level string cosmology and M-theory asymptotics.
Extracted six explicit open problems from subsections 3.1-3.6 on alpha-prime corrections, interacting fluids, and 11-dimensional supergravity stability.
Extracted six explicit open problems from subsections 4.1-4.6 on braneworld asymptotics, genericity, and Milne-state stability in ekpyrotic/cyclic scenarios.

Accepted the explicitly enumerated project statements in sections 2-4; moved four later implicit research directions to needs_review because the source flags them only as under investigation, future work, unclear relation, or presently unknown rather than as fully formulated standalone problems.
